subject: Latency gate review + tech clarifications (p95/p99 targets, streaming)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/streaming qualification

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Sanjay — appreciate you and Tara carving out the time. Quick recap of the outcomes and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary success criteria: p95 end-to-end latency <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms for your low-latency interactive assistant workload.
- Current provider (your shared numbers): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~900ms (see attached spreadsheet).
- Constraints: burst concurrency up to 250 concurrent interactive sessions during peak, sustained throughput ~120 req/s. Streaming responses used for partial incrementality (server-sent events).
- Non-functional asks: request tracing/headers to correlate requests to user sessions, and token-level cost visibility for a 1-week POC.

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed on:
1) Redwood test harness: we'll provide an instruction doc + small script to replay sampled traffic and generate streaming sessions. Ben will attach the instructions by EOD.
2) You share a sanitized sample of 30 representative prompts and the current provider traces (we received the spreadsheet attached) so we can mirror payload shape and tokenization.
3) Technical kickoff: set up a 60-minute lab session this week to stand up a short POC run (traffic mirroring against hosted endpoint + our tracing).
4) Acceptance gating: we will classify results as PASS if p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms over a 24-hour sustained run at 80% peak load. Otherwise we flag regressions and iterate on batching/quantization.

Ben/G: please see the attached harness doc — Ben, can you call out what we need from Veridian (headers, auth, target concurrency) in reply?

Sanjay/Tara — are you available for the lab kickoff on Wednesday 11/4 at 10:00 PT? If not, propose two windows.

Thanks — Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-test-harness-instructions.md (text), veridian-current-provider-metrics.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Liu <tara@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/streaming qualification

Thanks Lauren — clear recap and the targets look right. A couple clarifications from our side before the lab: 

- The current provider metrics are from a 48-hour window, mixed traffic. We'll extract a strict interactive-only slice and share by EOD.
- For streaming, we use chunked SSE with average chunk size ~12 tokens; we can provide a sample SSE stream.
- Auth: we'll create a limited-scope API key for the POC and send it via your SecOps channel.

Wednesday 11/4 10:00 PT works for Tara and me. We'll be joined by our SRE (Tara) and one engineer who owns the client SDK.

One ask: can Redwood enable request-level trace IDs in the test harness so we can map traces back to our telemetry? We want to ensure apples-to-apples comparisons.

—Sanjay

On a side note, our legal team will need the SLA language if we move past POC; happy to have a later conversation on that.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/streaming qualification

Thanks, team — attaching the harness instructions (see attachment stub). Key technical clarifications / ask list from Redwood infra side:

1) Traffic profile we need from Veridian:
   - Representative QPS distribution (per minute bins) for peak hour
   - Session concurrency expectation (250 peak concurrent sessions, 120 sustained req/s as discussed)
   - Typical prompt sizes (median tokens, 90th percentile tokens) — we need these to tune KV cache behavior and batching thresholds.

2) Streaming specifics:
   - Confirm SSE vs Websocket (Sanjay: you noted SSE) and the average chunk latency you observe (time between chunks).
   - Do you require partial result ordering guarantees across tokens beyond standard streaming?

3) Benchmarking setup we will run:
   - A 24-hour sustained run at 80% of your peak QPS with a 5-minute warmup ramp.
   - We'll collect p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end (client->Redwood->model->client) and token-level server timing.
   - We'll instrument traces with a provided header X-VDN-TRACE so you can correlate in Veridian telemetry.

4) Access & security:
   - Please provide a POC API key via your secure channel and a CIDR range for our short-lived test harness if you want to limit egress.

Acceptance criteria (proposal): PASS if p95 <= 300ms AND p99 <= 600ms over the 24-hour run; otherwise we produce an action log with prioritized optimizations (batching windows, quantization profile, routing to a lower-latency instance pool).

I'll flag a few likely tuning knobs after the first 1-hour run; those usually move p99 more than p95.

Lauren — I'll join the Wed 10:00 PT kickoff and bring the infra laptop.

--
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment stub: redwood-test-harness-instructions.md

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@veridian.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Liu <tara@veridian.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/streaming qualification

Perfect — thanks Ben. We just dropped the interactive-only slice and the 30 sanitized prompts into the Drive link (shared to lauren@redwood.ai). We've also created a scoped API key and sent it to your SecOps address.

Quick confirmations:
- SSE confirmed; chunk interval averages 45ms on our edge, chunk sizes 6-18 tokens.
- We'll accept the proposed acceptance criteria for the POC. If we see regressions at p99 we'll expect a 48-hour remediation cadence and at minimum a rollback path.

See you Wednesday at 10:00 PT — Tara will kick off the session and give the SRE access to our tracing.

—Sanjay
